newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate up 10 bps to 10.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate up 10 bps to 10.4 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average lending rate inched up ten basis points to 10.4 percent on Wednesday, propelled by higher demand for fresh kuna funds.
Dealers said total settlements rose to 42.9 million kuna, of which 24.1 million was fresh borrowing. The end of trading left a surplus of 26.1 million kuna on the supply side.
Most of new loans were call money borrowings, granted at the steady rate of 9.0 percent.
Interbank rates ranged between 11.0 percent for fresh two-week funds and 15.0 percent for two-month loans.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Thursday slightly firmer at 5.4909 against the dollar and at 3.5625 versus the German mark. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
